Hi Susan — thanks for the details and the attachments. Looping in Ben (capacity SLA/product) and Stephanie (legal touchpoint).

Quick answers up-front:
- Sustained throughput: we can guarantee a sustained token throughput per reserved node class measured over 5-minute sliding windows and backed by credits if we miss the floor. We typically express this as tokens/sec per instance and a monthly uptime/throughput SLA.
- Priority lanes & soft preemption: reserved capacity is placed into a priority lane and preemption is limited to controlled, announced maintenance or extreme emergency fallbacks; "soft preemption windows" mean we provide a short (configurable) grace period where reserved requests are queued rather than evicted.
- Long-tail requests: we protect tenant isolation by keeping a bounded queue depth and offering optional background batching windows for large jobs (e.g., nightly batches) that trade latency for throughput.

Next steps: Ben, can you draft a concise amendment (2–3 pages) that maps our queueing behavior, crediting rules, and the measurement method so Susan can share with procurement/legal? I attached our standard starting draft (redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf) for reference.

Hi team — following up from Laura's ask, here's a focused technical summary you can drop into an amendment.

Measurement and credits
- We report tokens/sec per reserved instance over two windows: 5-minute sliding (short) and 60-minute rolling (smoothing). Credits for missed throughput are calculated against the 60-minute view by default (conservative), with the 5-minute used for alerting/operational triage.

Priority & queue behavior
- Reserved capacity receives priority lane classification. Incoming reserved requests are accepted into that lane until a configurable queue depth (default 1,000 inflight tokens equivalent per pool).
- If queue depth is reached, we enter a short headroom period (configurable, default 120s) during which we continue to accept requests but degrade to batching/backfill behavior (responses may be delayed).
- After headroom expires, we return a 429-like signal to the client advising fallback. We do not silently evict reserved requests mid-execution unless safety/maintenance is in effect.

Throughput guarantees & fallbacks
- Guaranteed baseline: X tokens/sec per instance for the selected reserved SKU (we will map X to Polaris' token profile in the amendment).
- Compensatory credits: when baseline is not met over the 60-minute window, we issue usage credits pro-rated to the missed tokens. Credits are applied to the next billing cycle.

Operational notes
- We will include a per-incident timeline and root cause report when credits are triggered. Exceptions for force-majeure are defined in Section 6 of the draft.

I'll fold this into a 2-page amendment and send a draft by EOD. For the alignment call, propose Monday 9/6 11:00am PT — Laura, can you confirm?

Ben
